entity.name: Marcel Proust
entity.description: Proust spent 14 years writing in a cork-lined room. French novelist who revolutionized stream-of-consciousness fiction. Author of the 7-volume 'In Search of Lost Time.' Died with the final volume still unfinished.

moment.name: Marcel Proust Buried With an Unfinished Masterpiece Still in His Desk
moment.subtitle: Cimetière Père-Lachaise, 16 Rue du Repos, Paris — black granite tomb, Division 85
moment.description: Marcel Proust died November 18, 1922, of pneumonia complicated by a lung abscess — refusing medical treatment to preserve his mental clarity for writing. He was 51. Buried at Père-Lachaise in a simple black granite tomb beside his parents, Proust had corrected galley proofs from his deathbed hours before dying. The final volume of his 4,000-page masterpiece was published posthumously, edited by his brother Robert.

entity.name: Gertrude Stein
entity.description: Gertrude Stein rewrote how English sentences think. The Oakland-born expatriate hosted Picasso, Hemingway, and Matisse in her Paris salon. Her last words were reportedly a question: 'What is the answer?'

moment.name: Gertrude Stein Buried Beneath a Stone That Tells Both Sides of a Love Story
moment.subtitle: Cimetière Père-Lachaise, 16 Rue du Repos, Paris — shared granite slab, Alice B. Toklas on the reverse
moment.description: Stein died July 27, 1946, of stomach cancer, hours after abdominal surgery at the American Hospital in Neuilly-sur-Seine. Buried in Division 94 of Père-Lachaise, the grave's front face bears Stein's name in bold serif type. The reverse — added in 1967 — names Alice B. Toklas, Stein's partner of 39 years. Two women, one stone, opposite sides: the monument's geometry quietly mirrors a lifetime of public invisibility.

entity.name: Michael Faraday
entity.description: Electricity's architect who never finished school. Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction, invented the electric motor, and coined the term 'ion.' Despite fame, he refused a knighthood and died a humble member of the Sandemanian church.

moment.name: Michael Faraday Buried Far From the Abbey That Wanted Him
moment.subtitle: Highgate Cemetery, Swain's Lane, Highgate — a plain white marble headstone, deliberately modest
moment.description: Michael Faraday died August 25, 1867, at Hampton Court, where Queen Victoria had granted him grace-and-favour residence. He was buried September 2 at Highgate Cemetery in a Sandemanian plot — the small Christian sect he served as elder. Westminster Abbey offered a grave beside Newton, but Faraday declined in advance. The man who unlocked the electromagnetic age rests under a stone that lists only his name and dates.
moment.address: Highgate Cemetery, Highgate, England, United Kingdom

entity.name: Alexander Litvinenko
entity.description: Poisoned spy whose death exposed Kremlin's reach. Former FSB officer turned MI6 informant, killed by radioactive polonium-210 slipped into a London teacup. His deathbed photo became one of the most haunting images of Cold War's long shadow.

moment.name: Alexander Litvinenko Buried Under Armed Guard After Polonium Poisoning
moment.subtitle: Highgate Cemetery, Swain's Lane, Highgate — grave sealed in lead-lined coffin
moment.description: Alexander Litvinenko died November 23, 2006, three weeks after drinking polonium-210-laced tea at London's Millennium Hotel. So radioactive was the corpse that undertakers required special protective equipment and the coffin was sealed in lead before burial at Highgate. A British public inquiry later concluded Vladimir Putin 'probably approved' the assassination — making Litvinenko's grave, in effect, a monument to state-sanctioned murder on British soil.
moment.address: Highgate Cemetery, Highgate, England, United Kingdom

entity.name: Judy Garland
entity.description: Hollywood's most tragic star never stopped performing. Born Frances Gumm in 1922, Garland conquered MGM at 16 as Dorothy in The Wizard of Oz. Decades of studio-mandated pills, five marriages, and a voice that could shatter silence defined her 47 years.

moment.name: Judy Garland Finally Comes Home to Hollywood — 22 Years After She Left It
moment.subtitle: Hollywood Forever Cemetery, 6000 Santa Monica Blvd — white marble crypt inside the Judy Garland Memorial
moment.description: Garland died June 22, 1969 in London — a barbiturate overdose ruled accidental. The woman who embodied Hollywood was buried 5,400 miles from it. In 1995, her remains were relocated to Hollywood Forever Cemetery, where a dedicated memorial now draws fans who leave ruby slippers at the crypt. The girl who sang about somewhere over the rainbow spent 26 years buried in New York.
moment.address: Hollywood Forever Cemetery, Los Angeles, California, United States

entity.name: Cecil B. DeMille
entity.description: Hollywood's original showman rewrote cinema's rules. DeMille directed 70 films over 50 years, invented the Hollywood epic, and produced The Ten Commandments twice. His last film grossed more than any movie in history at the time of release.

moment.name: Cecil B. DeMille Buried Yards From the Studio Where He Built Hollywood
moment.subtitle: Hollywood Forever Cemetery, 6000 Santa Monica Blvd — a modest flat granite slab among legends
moment.description: Cecil B. DeMille died of heart failure on January 21, 1959, just months after completing The Ten Commandments re-release tour. The director who staged chariot races, parted seas, and commanded casts of thousands was buried beneath a restrained flat granite marker at Hollywood Forever — a cemetery literally sharing a wall with Paramount Pictures, the studio DeMille helped found. The king of spectacle chose silence.
moment.address: Hollywood Forever Cemetery, Los Angeles, California, United States

entity.name: Douglas Fairbanks
entity.description: Silent film's first action hero redefined stardom. Fairbanks co-founded United Artists with Chaplin and Pickford, pioneered the celebrity marriage as spectacle, and performed his own death-defying stunts across 40+ films.

moment.name: Douglas Fairbanks Buried Beneath a Reflecting Pool His Son Commissioned
moment.subtitle: Hollywood Forever Cemetery, 6000 Santa Monica Blvd — marble tomb flanked by a long ornamental pool
moment.description: Douglas Fairbanks died of a heart attack on December 12, 1939, aged 56 — his body worn down by decades of performing his own stunts. Initially interred at Forest Lawn, Fairbanks was moved to Hollywood Forever in 1959 when son Douglas Jr. commissioned an elaborate marble tomb with a reflecting pool. The man who once leapt across castle walls now rests in the most theatrical grave in a cemetery full of them.
moment.address: Hollywood Forever Cemetery, Los Angeles, California, United States

entity.name: Johnny Ramone
entity.description: Punk rock's most disciplined guitarist never missed a show. Co-founded the Ramones in 1974, pioneered three-chord punk with downstroke-only playing, performed 2,263 concerts without a single cancellation.

moment.name: Johnny Ramone Buried Beneath a Bronze Effigy Holding His Mosrite Guitar
moment.subtitle: Hollywood Forever Cemetery, 6000 Santa Monica Blvd — life-size bronze sculpture marks the plot
moment.description: Johnny Ramone (John Cummings) died September 15, 2004, after a five-year battle with prostate cancer, aged 55. Buried at Hollywood Forever Cemetery, the grave is crowned by a life-size bronze sculpture of Johnny mid-performance, guitar raised. The irony: a registered Republican and self-described conservative, Johnny rests eternally in Hollywood — the industry he openly disdained — surrounded by the film legends he outlasted.
moment.address: Hollywood Forever Cemetery, Los Angeles, California, United States

entity.name: Mickey Rooney
entity.description: Child star who never stopped performing. Rooney appeared in over 300 films across nine decades, earned four honorary Oscars, and was once the highest-paid actor in Hollywood. Married eight times — a record even Tinseltown struggled to top.

moment.name: Mickey Rooney Buried Among the Legends He Outlived
moment.subtitle: Hollywood Forever Cemetery, 6000 Santa Monica Blvd — flat bronze marker flush with the lawn
moment.description: Mickey Rooney died April 6, 2014, at 93, still working — his final film released posthumously. The boy who debuted at 17 months old was interred at Hollywood Forever, the cemetery he'd driven past for decades on the way to studio lots. A legal battle over his estate erupted almost immediately after death, with estranged family members contesting his final wishes. His simple bronze grave marker offers no epitaph — remarkable restraint for a man who was never once offstage.
moment.address: Hollywood Forever Cemetery, Los Angeles, California, United States

entity.name: Irving Berlin
entity.description: He wrote 'White Christmas' — the best-selling single ever recorded. Russian-born immigrant Irving Berlin composed over 1,500 songs, shaping American music for seven decades. Berlin lived to 101, outlasting nearly everyone who made him famous.

moment.name: Irving Berlin Buried Quietly After 101 Years of Writing America's Soundtrack
moment.subtitle: Woodlawn Cemetery, 4199 Webster Ave, Bronx — granite headstone shared with wife Ellin
moment.description: Irving Berlin died September 22, 1989, in his Manhattan townhouse, having spent his final years as a recluse who refused visitors and unplugged his phone. The man who wrote 'God Bless America' received a private burial at Woodlawn Cemetery in the Bronx — no public ceremony, no fanfare. The irony is sharp: Berlin's songs defined American celebration for a century, yet the composer himself chose total silence at the end.
moment.address: Woodlawn Cemetery, Bronx, New York, United States

entity.name: Elizabeth Cady Stanton
entity.description: Suffragist who rewrote what women could demand. Drafted the 1848 Declaration of Sentiments, co-founded the women's suffrage movement, and authored The Woman's Bible. Died 18 years before women won the vote she spent 54 years fighting for.

moment.name: Elizabeth Cady Stanton Buried 18 Years Before the Victory She Never Saw
moment.subtitle: Woodlawn Cemetery, 4199 Webster Ave, Bronx, NY — shared plot with husband Henry Stanton
moment.description: Elizabeth Cady Stanton died on October 26, 1902, at her Manhattan apartment, aged 86 — just days after writing a letter to President Theodore Roosevelt demanding women's suffrage. Buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in the Bronx alongside husband Henry Stanton, a man who famously left her suffrage convention early out of embarrassment. The 19th Amendment passed in 1920, eighteen years too late.
moment.address: Woodlawn Cemetery, Bronx, New York, United States

entity.name: Joseph Pulitzer
entity.description: Blind press baron who invented modern journalism. Hungarian immigrant Joseph Pulitzer built a newspaper empire on sensationalism and social crusades. His will endowed the prize bearing his name — awarded annually since 1917.

moment.name: Joseph Pulitzer Buried in Silence — the Deaf-Blind Mogul Who Never Stopped Shouting
moment.subtitle: Woodlawn Cemetery, 4199 Webster Ave, Bronx, NY — granite mausoleum with bronze doors
moment.description: Joseph Pulitzer died aboard his yacht Liberty off Charleston Harbor on October 29, 1911, dictating dispatches to the end. The man who weaponized noise — screaming headlines, yellow journalism, the Spanish-American War — spent his final decade in near-total sensory isolation, tormented by sound. His Woodlawn mausoleum, sealed behind bronze doors, holds the architect of American mass media in permanent, ironic quiet.
moment.address: Woodlawn Cemetery, Bronx, New York, United States

entity.name: Fiorello La Guardia
entity.description: New York's most beloved mayor never stopped fighting. Fiorello La Guardia served three terms as NYC mayor (1934–1945), read comics on radio during a newspaper strike, and stood just 5'2" — earning the nickname 'The Little Flower.'

moment.name: La Guardia Buried Quietly in the Bronx Borough He Championed
moment.subtitle: Woodlawn Cemetery, 4199 Webster Ave, Bronx — modest flat granite marker beneath an oak canopy
moment.description: Fiorello La Guardia died September 20, 1947, of pancreatic cancer at age 64 — just two years after leaving City Hall. The man who had personally directed traffic, raced to fire scenes, and declared war on slot machines was buried with little fanfare at Woodlawn Cemetery. The irony: La Guardia, who championed the poor his entire career, rests among Gilded Age tycoons including Jay Gould and F.W. Woolworth.
moment.address: Woodlawn Cemetery, Bronx, New York, United States

entity.name: Leonard Bernstein
entity.description: Conductor who made classical music electric. Bernstein led the New York Philharmonic for 11 years, composed West Side Story, and taught millions through televised Young People's Concerts. Died clutching a cigarette — fittingly theatrical to the last.

moment.name: Leonard Bernstein Is Buried With a Baton and a Score of Mahler's Ninth
moment.subtitle: Green-Wood Cemetery, 500 25th St, Brooklyn — a flat granite slab beneath an oak canopy
moment.description: Bernstein died October 14, 1990, of a heart attack accelerated by decades of smoking and relentless performance. Five days later, mourners carried his coffin through Brooklyn to Green-Wood. Per his wishes, a baton and a worn copy of Mahler's Ninth Symphony were placed inside the casket — the same score he had conducted at his final concert just four days before his death, barely able to breathe.
moment.address: Green-Wood Cemetery, Brooklyn, New York, United States

entity.name: Louis Comfort Tiffany
entity.description: Stained glass transformed into pure American obsession. Louis Comfort Tiffany revolutionized decorative arts with iridescent Favrile glass, the iconic lamp shades, and a design philosophy that blurred fine art with craft. His studio produced over 5,000 window designs.

moment.name: Louis Comfort Tiffany Buried Beneath Stone as Plain as His Work Was Ornate
moment.subtitle: Green-Wood Cemetery, 500 25th St, Brooklyn, NY — a modest family plot marker amid Victorian grandeur
moment.description: Louis Comfort Tiffany died January 17, 1933, aged 84, having outlived both his fortune and his fashion. The Art Nouveau wave had crashed; modernism dismissed his jeweled windows as gaudy excess. Green-Wood Cemetery received the man whose studio had glazed cathedrals across America — yet the Tiffany family plot marker is strikingly understated. The supreme irony: the artist who taught America to worship colored light now rests beneath stone that lets none through.
moment.address: Green-Wood Cemetery, Brooklyn, New York, United States
